label: L-05
title: An honest, correctly-registered stablecoin whose decimals() is not view is rejected by the new cross-check, stranding that pair's reward entitlement - and the minter's own mint path keeps working, so the failure is invisible to mint-path monitoring
titleNote: RETITLED FROM THE CLASSIFIER'S WORDING per the validity-checker's mandatory rescope. The classifier's title ('a token that cannot, or stops, answering decimals()') spanned three triggers, two of which are sponsor-intended design. The title now names only the reportable core: trigger T3 plus the detection asymmetry.
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Newly minted this run; verified to reproduce from fingerprintBasis and not to collide with any of the 19 pre-existing ledger fingerprints. The rescope narrows the reported triggers but does NOT change contract, function or rootCauseClass, so the fingerprint is unchanged by it.

reportableCore: (a) T3 - an HONEST, correctly-registered token whose decimals() is not declared `view` is rejected by STATICCALL with ok == false and reverts DecimalsUnavailable, even though its registration is correct and its answer would have MATCHED. PoC-proven.

(b) THE DETECTION ASYMMETRY - PhusdStableMinter.mint keeps working for that same token because it reads only its own stored config.decimals at minter:254 and never queries the token. The mint-path smoke test therefore passes green while the antimatter product is dead.

demotedToDocumentedContext.T1: A registered upgradeable stablecoin stops answering decimals() after an implementation change.
demotedToDocumentedContext.T2: The owner registers an old-style token that never had decimals() at all.
demotedToDocumentedContext.ruling: SPONSOR-INTENDED DESIGN, ON THE RECORD. NOT reported as defects. story-002's 'Why not try/catch' section (lines 129-160) enumerates empty return data (a token with a permissive fallback and no decimals()), an address with no code, and a reverting decimals(), and states: 'Both approaches fail closed, which is the security property.' Reporting T1/T2 as defects would flag intended design as a bug. They are retained below only as context for the registration checklist.

rescope.whyThisDoesNotWeakenTheFinding: T3 is the trigger the classifier itself called 'the one that matters', is the only leg carrying an honest-token argument, and is the leg the Low band already rested on. The band is unaffected by the rescope.

mechanismCorrection.claim: THE MECHANISM IS NOT THE STATICCALL.
mechanismCorrection.detail: `toStableAmount` is declared `public view`, so a state-mutating decimals() fails IDENTICALLY under try/catch. Switching from a raw staticcall to try/catch would not admit a T3 token. The defect is that the design places a liveness dependency on a third-party token's metadata being callable in a view context at settlement time, not that a particular call form was chosen. story-002's justification for preferring a raw staticcall over try/catch (an uncatchable uint8 decode of a >255 value) stands and is not challenged here.

classification.assetImpact: NO LOSS, DELAYED REALISATION. Antimatter is inert held alone; its entire value is the phUSD that annihilation emits. While the condition persists, that already-distributed reward entitlement cannot be realised against the affected stablecoin. The revert happens in toStableAmount (reached from :230), strictly BEFORE _burn at :239 and before any transfer, so no antimatter is burned, no stablecoin is pulled and no phUSD is minted. A holder who chooses to exit during the outage does so at whatever discount the market applies to a temporarily unredeemable claim - a market consequence of an outage, not a protocol loss, and not counted as value leak here.
attackPath: NO ATTACKER IS REQUIRED - this is a liveness/configuration hazard and is classified as one.

1. The owner registers stablecoin S on PhusdStableMinter with the CORRECT decimals value (say 18). S is honest: it implements decimals(), it answers 18, and its transfer/approve/balance semantics are entirely standard. Its decimals() is simply not declared `view` - it increments a read counter, lazily caches, or emits.

2. Any call to toStableAmount(S, x) reaches the staticcall at :292. STATICCALL rejects the state-mutating callee, so ok == false, and :293 reverts DecimalsUnavailable(S) - despite the registered value and the token's own answer AGREEING.
3. Every annihilate(S, ...) therefore reverts, for every holder, permanently, until the configuration changes.

4. DETECTION ASYMMETRY: PhusdStableMinter.mint(S, ...) continues to work perfectly, because the minter reads its own stored config.decimals at minter:254 and never queries the token's metadata. A mint-path smoke test passes green while the antimatter product is dead for that pair.
5. Recovery: the owner registers a working alternative stablecoin, or holders pair against any other already-registered one.
classification.likelihood: LOW for the condition arising; LOW for it becoming PERMANENT. T3 is proven reachable and requires no misbehaviour by anyone, but no stablecoin currently of interest implements decimals() as non-view (see decidingEvidence). T3 is a registration-time property that the very first annihilate against that token exposes - PROVIDED anyone calls annihilate, which is exactly what the detection asymmetry makes uncertain. Permanence additionally requires an owner who never responds, which Law 3's trusted, non-malicious owner does not license as an assumption.
classification.assumptions: STATED IN FULL. (a) A registered stablecoin's decimals() is not callable in a static (view) context, while its registration and its answer are both correct. (b) FOR THE SEVERE CASE ONLY: that stablecoin is the sole registered one, or the affected holders hold only that one. (c) FOR PERMANENCE ONLY: the owner does not promptly register an alternative. Assumptions (b) and (c) are NOT established at c91bc1a.
classification.externalRequirements: A third-party token's metadata implementation, which the protocol does not control.

c4Criterion: QA/Low - state handling / operational-configuration hazard. The C4 Medium clause 'the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted' IS engaged on its face and is declined on the likelihood of the triggering configuration, not on mechanism. The value-leak limb of Medium is not engaged at all.
law3Verdict: FOOTGUN, IN SCOPE. The owner would reasonably assume the minter's own registered `decimals` field is the authority - that is why the minter carries the field - and would be surprised both that annihilation additionally requires the token to self-report in a view context, and that the resulting failure is INVISIBLE on the minter path while fatal on the antimatter path. T3 is not an owner error at all. NOT classified on any 'malicious owner' basis.
justification: Held at LOW, but the band rests on ONE piece of evidence and nothing else (see decidingEvidence) and is CONDITIONAL ON A MUTABLE REGISTRY (see bandCondition). The Medium case was argued at full strength on the C4 availability limb. Two deflators carry it: the failure is fail-closed BEFORE the burn, so this is delayed realisation and not loss and the value-leak limb never engages; and `stable` is a free parameter, so holders route around the affected token whenever a second stablecoin is registered. The compound case that would make this a genuine protocol-wide outage - sole registered stablecoin, no replacement - is a conjunction of terms none of which is observed at HEAD, and an unobserved conjunction is what C4 means by a hypothetical. What keeps it at the TOP of Low rather than the bottom is the detection asymmetry confirmed against PhusdStableMinter:254: the mint path keeps working for the same token, so the standard smoke test passes while the antimatter product is dead. That detection gap is newly introduced by this delta - at 0bb82d8 toStableAmount made no call to `stable` at all - and it argues for the escalation trigger below rather than for a comfortable closure now. This is deliberately NOT deflated to keep the report tidy: it is flagged borderline and given an evidence-based route to Medium.

struck.whyStruck: INAPPLICABLE TO C4's AVAILABILITY LIMB. C4 Medium reads 'assets are not at direct risk, but the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted'. The clause is written to cover exactly the case where nothing is consumed; citing non-consumption against it argues the wrong limb.

CONTRADICTS THIS FINDING'S OWN EVIDENCE. Recovery in one transaction presupposes the owner KNOWS service is down. The detection asymmetry - leg (b) of the reportable core - is the finding's assertion that they would not: the mint path stays green. A deflator cannot rest on the premise the finding disproves.

retained: Fail-closed before the burn: delayed realisation, not loss; the value-leak limb of Medium never engages.
`stable` is a free parameter: holders route around the affected token whenever a second stablecoin is registered.

decidingEvidence.why: RECORDED EXPLICITLY BECAUSE THE LOW BAND RESTS ON THIS AND NOTHING ELSE. If this evidence is wrong or goes stale, the band moves.

primary.content: 'every stablecoin of interest exposes decimals()', with DecimalsUnavailable framed as a defensive guard against a FUTURE registration rather than as a live condition.
primary.weight: This is the whole basis for treating the triggering configuration as unlikely. It is an attestation about the CURRENT registered set, not a property of the code.

decidingEvidence.corroboration: Staging registers USDC (6dp), DOLA (18dp) and USDe (18dp), all with standard `view` decimals() getters. None of the three is a T3 token.
decidingEvidence.fragility: Neither the attestation nor the corroboration constrains a FUTURE registration. Both describe a set that one transaction can change.

bandCondition.flag: CONDITIONAL ON A MUTABLE REGISTRY - FLAGGED FOR HUMAN TRIAGE
bandCondition.statement: This Low is conditional, not settled. It flips to Medium on a single registration transaction: registering one stablecoin whose decimals() does not answer a STATICCALL is sufficient, and nothing in the code prevents it or reports it. The band is a statement about the registry's current contents, which the protocol does not freeze, and not about the code - which is unchanged in every configuration.
bandCondition.triageAsk: A human should decide whether to accept a severity that depends on a mutable configuration, or to require the registration-time check (see recommendation) that makes the band unconditional.

escalateToMediumIf: PRIMARY TRIGGER: any stablecoin is registered on Antimatter's minter whose decimals() does not answer a STATICCALL with exactly 32 bytes. VERIFY BY CALLING toStableAmount(S, 1e18) AT REGISTRATION TIME - the mint path cannot detect this, because PhusdStableMinter.mint reads only its own stored config.decimals at minter:254 and never queries the token.
Any future change moves the toStableAmount call after _burn, so a revert can strand consumed assets.

strickenEscalationTrigger.struck: 'Exactly ONE stablecoin is registered on the minter Antimatter points at while antimatter is being distributed as a staking reward - this alone moves it to Medium.'
strickenEscalationTrigger.whyStruck: It TESTS THE WRONG CONDITION and IS NOT CHECKABLE. Wrong condition: a sole registered stablecoin is dangerous only if that stablecoin is also a T3 token - a registry of one healthy stablecoin is not this finding at all, while a registry of five stablecoins one of which is T3 IS this finding for every holder paired against it. Not checkable: it asks a future triager to establish a distribution-programme fact about staking rewards that no artifact in this repo records. The replacement trigger tests the actual defect and is verifiable with a single eth_call.

recommendation.primary: CROSS-CHECK ONCE AT REGISTRATION/ACCEPTANCE TIME ON ANTIMATTER'S SIDE, AND CACHE THE RESULT. Verify the token's decimals() against the minter's registered value when the stablecoin is accepted, store the verified value, and read the cached value on the settlement path. This fixes T3 - a token that answers correctly once is never rejected later for how it answers - without introducing any fail-open branch, and it converts a settlement-time liveness dependency into a one-time registration-time check. It also makes the escalation trigger above impossible to satisfy silently.
recommendation.secondaryIfAcceptedAsIs: Document the operational requirement that decimals() must be callable in a static context, add it to the registration checklist, keep at least two independently-implemented stablecoins registered at all times, widen the DecimalsUnavailable NatSpec (which today says only 'does not report usable decimals at all') to say 'through a static call', and run a monitor that calls toStableAmount(S, 1e18) per registered S - the mint path cannot detect this failure.

rejectedRecommendation.text: 'Treat an UNAVAILABLE decimals() as no independent confirmation available and fall back to the minter's registered value, keeping the hard revert only for a decimals() that answers and DISAGREES.'
rejectedRecommendation.status: REMOVED AS PRIMARY. MUST NOT SHIP AS THE HEADLINE MITIGATION.
rejectedRecommendation.reason: It RE-OPENS EXACTLY THE FAIL-OPEN PATH THAT LEDGER M-01 (a1c81428a47ad295, fix-pending) EXISTS TO CLOSE, for every token that can make its decimals() unavailable - which a lying token controls. story-002 chose fail-closed deliberately and named it 'the security property'. Reversing a story-sanctioned security property is an OWNER DECISION, not a mitigation line, and must be raised as such rather than slipped into a recommendations list.

doNotCollapse.reason: Same call site, same delta. L-04 needs a hostile or broken token and is defence-in-depth; L-05 is reachable by an honest token and is an operational hazard.
doNotCollapse.fixIndependence: THIS FINDING'S FIX DOES NOT FIX L-04. `bytes memory data` at :292 copies all returndata BEFORE any check, so moving the cross-check to registration time leaves the unbounded copy in place on every call that still performs one. Conversely, bounding the copy does not make an unavailable decimals() available. BOTH FIXES ARE OWED.

interactionWithM01: The cross-check this finding critiques IS the fix for ledger M-01 (a1c81428a47ad295, fix-pending), and Tier-3 INV6 plus Halmos SYM-2 confirm it closes M-01's exploit path in both directions. This finding is the COST of that fix, not an argument to revert it - which is precisely why the fail-open fallback was removed from the recommendation.
boundaryNote: Per MR-02-P3 and WATCH-02-03, M-01's closure is BOUNDARY-SCOPED - correct for Antimatter, silent for PhusdStableMinter's own permissionless mint. That warning is carried by MR-02-P3 and WATCH-02-03 and is not restated as a finding here.

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues authority on this project. 'Reckless admin mistake' declined: T3 involves no owner error whatsoever - the registration is correct and the registered value matches the token's own answer, and the call still reverts.

validityCheck.weirdErc20Ruling: CARVE-OUT DECLINED after reasoning rather than label-matching. decimals() is an OPTIONAL part of EIP-20, so a token without it is standard-conformant, not weird. T3's token is stronger still: it implements decimals(), answers 18, and is registered as 18 - its answer is CORRECT and matches, and nothing about its transfer, approve or balance semantics is non-standard. The design also self-refutes the carve-out: PhusdStableMinter carries an explicit registered `decimals` field precisely because the protocol does not want to depend on token self-report.
validityCheck.intentionalDesignRuling: DETECTED, SCOPED TO T1 AND T2 ONLY. Those are now demoted to documented context. T3 is NOT covered by story-002: the story never considers a decimals() that is non-view, and the failure there is not the staticcall at all.
validityCheck.recommendation: Keep in the QA bundle, rescoped to (a)+(b), with the recommendation reordered.

additionalContext.rootCause: The settlement path places a per-call liveness dependency on a third-party token's metadata being callable in a view context. `toStableAmount` is `public view`, so any decimals() that is not itself view fails, regardless of call form.
additionalContext.newInThisDelta: YES. At 0bb82d8 toStableAmount made no external call to `stable` at all; the dependency is introduced by story-002 (f48f30d) as the fix for ledger M-01.
additionalContext.documentedContextNotReported: T1 (a registered upgradeable token stops answering decimals()) and T2 (an old-style token that never had decimals()) both fail closed BY DESIGN per story-002 lines 129-160, which enumerates empty returndata, a codeless address and a reverting decimals() and states 'Both approaches fail closed, which is the security property.' They belong on the registration checklist, not in the findings list.
